title: Econ Helmsman: Initiative cycle cadence and rollout plan for cost optimization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Create a repeatable initiative template (the 'Econ Helmsman') for running cross-functional cost-optimization cycles that coordinate batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization experiments across Dedicated and Hosted populations. This ticket tracks the roadmap, success criteria, sprint cadence, governance, and rollout guardrails for the next two quarters.
objectives: 1) Reduce per-token cost on tiered workloads by 18% (end-to-end) across target customers. 2) Validate >95% quality parity on benchmark prompts when applying quantization + batch policy. 3) Establish an operational cadence and template for future econ cycles with clear ownership and rollback paths.
okrs: O1: Launch Econ Helmsman cycle and run three live experiments (batching policy A/B, KV-ttl tuning, 4-bit quant profile) by 2026-05-15. KR1: Achieve >=12% cost reduction in at least one experiment combined with <3% quality degradation. KR2: Create console dashboard widget for token-econ KPIs. O2: Standardize playbook so PM/Eng/Design can run cycles with <2 week onboarding.
milestones: 2026-03-20: Experiment matrix and measurement plan finalized
2026-04-05: First canary (batching deferral policy) live on 5% traffic
2026-04-22: KV-prefetch TTL variants rolled to 25% with monitoring
2026-05-15: Quantization profile validation complete; review decision
2026-06-01: Consolidated rollout to Dedicated pools and hosted low-tier
tasks: Draft experiment matrix (batch size, max latency budget, cache TTL, quant profile)
Define evaluation prompts and automated quality checks (PM + Applied ML)
Implement console dashboard with token-econ widgets and per-route attribution
Create canary orchestrator config and safeties (auto-fallback on regression)
Coordinate Dedicated capacity owners for controlled rollouts
Write rollout runbooks and rollback criteria for each experiment
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment definitions include clear success/failure thresholds and measurement queries. 2) Console exposes token-econ metrics at route/model granularity. 3) At least one experiment produces >=12% cost improvement without failing quality thresholds. 4) Playbook document exists and team trained.
decisions: Decision 2026-03-08: Use conservative quantization first (4-bit with per-layer outlier handling) for Hosted non-critical traffic.
Decision 2026-03-18: Start with latency-SLO-aware batching (max latency 120ms p95) rather than throughput-only batching to protect UX.
Decision 2026-03-25: KV cache TTL experimentation will be opt-in per-customer via feature flags; default remains current TTL until validated.
risks: Quality regressions caused by quantization across edge-case prompts
User-visible latency spikes if batching thresholds are miscalibrated
Capacity contention in Dedicated pools during larger rollouts
Insufficient telemetry to attribute cost wins to individual knobs
mitigations: Add per-prompt holdout evaluation and automated threshold-based rollback
Guard batching with p95 latency SLA and progressive traffic ramp
Reserve burst capacity windows with infra and schedule rollouts during low utilization
Instrument additional tags on requests to map savings to experiments
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): run experiments against synthetic/QA traffic and verify metrics. Phase 1 (Canary): 5% of non-enterprise hosted traffic for 2 weeks. Auto-fallback on >2% quality regression or p95 latency > 150ms. Phase 2 (Scale): expand to 25% with staggered Dedicated pool rollouts. Phase 3 (Consolidate): merge successful knobs into default serving profiles and update docs and SDK flags.
communication: Weekly status update in #econ-helmsman (Slack) and bi-weekly review with Eng leads and Applied ML. Exec summary to GTM/Support at milestone completions.
open_questions: What is the QPS boundary where batching begins to harm tail latency for short prompts? (Action: bench in ENG-4198)
Should we expose quant profile as a per-tenant knob or keep it server-side-only? (Trade-off: control vs complexity)
What SLO guardrail should trigger automatic rollback for Dedicated customers with contractual SLAs?
